# F258 B1: deployed AFTER for PR 312

PR 312 merged as `7a6b8cbc8a7432b1f13e92ad39f0c329d76faca8` on
November 21, 2026, at 08:00:30 UTC. The measured daemon is PID 43526,
build `pij-rs 0.1.0`, commit `7a6b8cbc8a`, process start
November 21, 2026, 18:07:29 local time (UTC+10).
Read-only inspection confirmed schema version 48 and seats_by_pane.

**The requested deployed AFTER is measured; no aggregate whoami latency
improvement is demonstrated.** BEFORE was 2.106 ms active/completion;
the initial AFTER was 5.838 ms and one additional AFTER was 2.265 ms.
Both are retained. Refusals, workload, daemon age and host load differ,
so neither a feature-attributed latency regression nor an exclusive CPU
saving is established. The pre-deploy SQL-copy receipt remains valid;
it is not a deployed latency or CPU receipt.

## Matched 60-second protocol

The same session-local pr312_probe.py live command was run with
`nice -n 19 python3`, unchanged from BEFORE. Each edge reads
`pij-rs --json ping`, then single-PID
`/bin/ps -p <pid> -o lstart=,time=,rss=`, and queries only harness counts
among untombstoned seats through a mode=ro SQLite connection.
Elapsed time is monotonic; PID, start identity and deployed commit
must stay equal inside each window. The machine sampler is separate.
No bounce, local build, product edit or probe write to the live DB occurred.

active_us is active wall time across the route, including scheduling and
both ok and refused outcomes; it is not SQLite CPU or successful-only
latency. The aggregate cannot separate the refusals' share. Daemon CPU
is cumulative process CPU without exited-child CPU, not exclusive whoami
CPU. Registry cohorts are untombstoned rows, not a liveness census or a
count of active status-line consumers.

All other sites were flat. Each site's delta reconciles to the exact
total. The index introduces no new launch site; existing lifecycle and

## Separate machine sampler

The same `just spawn-rate --seconds 20 --json` recipe ran at niceness 19.
BEFORE: 20.0 s, PID 31125, 269.3 total new processes/s, sampled 250.9/s,
daemon-attributed lower bound 0.4/s.

AFTER: November 21, 2026, 08:10:30.354 -> 08:10:50.589 UTC,
20.0 s inner sample, PID 43526, **257.3 total new processes/s**,
sampled 241.4/s, no daemon children caught by the sampler.
Load 1/5/15 min at the outer edges:
45.158 / 52.298 / 57.444 -> 58.133 / 54.607 / 58.142.
The sampler's parent attribution is a lower bound, so an empty daemon
sample does not establish zero launches. The script-marker statusline
count misses exec'd native statusline processes. Neither machine sample
overlapped a 60-second CPU window. The 269.3 -> 257.3 change is an
uncontrolled fleet observation, not an index-attributed launch reduction.
